name: deckard-notes
description: Find your replicants, chase down loose ends, and keep your memories in order.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with Deckard
walkthroughs.description: Index the Markdown notes you already write, then follow the people, projects, and tasks in them.

steps.title: Open or create a note
steps.description:
Deckard indexes every saved Markdown file in the workspace. Start today's note, then write a line or two — or start from seven notes already written the way Deckard reads them.
[Create today's note](command:deckard.createDailyNote)
[Create a sample workspace](command:deckard.createSampleWorkspace)

steps.title: Tag what the note is about
steps.description:
Write a tag such as #project/atlas on a heading or a task, or @dana for a person. Tags are what Deckard connects notes by.
[Open Help](command:deckard.showHelp)

steps.title: See the workspace
steps.description:
Home collects today's note, your tasks, what is due, and the searches you keep.
[Open the Dashboard](command:deckard.showDashboard)

steps.title: Find anything
steps.description:
Find searches as you type. A search page holds the whole result, and Refine narrows it.
[Find a note](command:deckard.searchWorkspace)

viewsWelcome.contents:
Open a Markdown note to see its headings here.
[Create today's note](command:deckard.createDailyNote)
[Open Help](command:deckard.showHelp)

Your open tasks appear here, grouped by when they are wanted.

Write one in a note as a checklist item, or capture one without leaving the editor.
[Capture a task](command:deckard.capture)
[Open the Task Board](command:deckard.showTaskBoard)

languageModelTools.name: deckard_query
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search the workspace's Markdown notes and tasks with a Deckard query.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Searches the user's local Markdown notes and checklist tasks, as indexed by the Deckard extension, with a Deckard query, and returns the matching note sections and tasks with their workspace-relative paths, one-based lines, and headings; tasks include their state, due date, and priority. Use it to answer questions about the user's notes, projects, people, and to-dos. For example, 'open tasks for Atlas' is tag = #project/atlas AND task = open, and 'what is overdue' is task = open AND due < today. Conditions combine with AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Fields: tag (tag = #project/atlas; tag = #risk/* matches a namespace; a bare #tag or @person also works), text (text ~ "vendor" matches words in note and task text), task (open, done, or any; only tasks match), due, scheduled, and start (a date such as 2026-09-20, today, tomorrow, a window such as 7d counted forward, or none), done (done = 7d means completed in the last seven days), priority (highest, high, medium, none, low, lowest; priority >= high), kind (an entity namespace such as project or person), file and path (with * and ? wildcards), created and updated (dates or windows such as 30d). Shorthands: is:open, is:done, is:overdue, is:due (open and due within seven days), is:task, is:note, has:due and no:due (also scheduled, start, done, priority), and in:folder for a folder and everything in it. Operators are = != ~ !~ > >= < <=. If you do not know a tag's exact name, call deckard_list_tags first.

query.description: A Deckard query, such as tag = #project/atlas AND task = open.

limit.description: The most notes, and the most tasks, to return. Defaults to 25; totals always count every match.

sort.description: Order by title, or newest created or updated first. Otherwise tasks are listed open first and soonest due first.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_list_tags
languageModelTools.userDescription: List the tags used in the workspace's Markdown notes, most used first.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Lists the tags in the user's local Markdown notes, as indexed by the Deckard extension, most used first, with how many entries use each. Tags look like #project/atlas, #topic/leadership, or @person-name. Use it to find the exact tag to pass to deckard_query, optionally narrowed by a search such as 'atlas' or 'project/'.

search.description: Only tags whose name contains this text, such as atlas or project/.

limit.description: The most tags to return. Defaults to 50.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_add_task
languageModelTools.displayName: Add a task to a Deckard note
languageModelTools.userDescription: Adds a task to today's note, or to a note you name, after showing you the line.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Adds a checklist task to one of the user's Markdown notes: to today's daily note, or to the note named by a workspace-relative path as deckard_query reports paths. Write the task's words as text; metadata may be written in them the way the user writes tasks, such as a due date 📅 2026-09-30, a priority ⏫, or a person 👤 @dana. Nothing is written until the user approves the exact line in a preview; the answer says whether it was written, and where. Use deckard_change_task to change a task that already exists.

text.description: The task's words, such as "Call Ren about the budget 📅 2026-09-30".

note.description: A workspace-relative note to add it to, such as notes/atlas.md. Today's daily note when absent.

languageModelTools.name: deckard_change_task
languageModelTools.displayName: Change a task in a Deckard note
languageModelTools.userDescription: Completes, reopens, retitles, dates, prioritizes, or hands over a task, after showing you the line.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Changes one existing checklist task, named by its note and one-based line as deckard_query reports them. Any of: title (new words), complete (true or false), due (YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear), priority (highest, high, medium, low, lowest, or null to clear), assignee (a person tag such as @dana, or null to clear). Only the fields given change; the rest of the line is kept as written. The change is refused if the line is no longer the task the index knows, so ask deckard_query first. Nothing is written until the user approves the exact line in a preview; the answer says whether it was written.

note.description: The task's note, workspace-relative, as deckard_query reports it.

line.description: The task's one-based line, as deckard_query reports it.

complete.description: true completes it, writing the done date; false reopens it.

due.description: A day as YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear the due date.

priority.description: The priority, or null to clear it.

assignee.description: Who the task is for, as their tag, or null to clear it.

deckard.notesFolder.description: Optional workspace-relative folder containing Markdown notes. Leave empty to index all Markdown files in the workspace.

enumDescriptions: A plain interface that takes its colors and fonts from your VS Code theme, light or dark.
Deckard's original replicant terminal interface.
A dark technical operations interface inspired by the Oblivion reference screens.
A warm, high-contrast interface inspired by LCARS from Star Trek: The Next Generation.
A neon grid interface inspired by 1980s synthwave and outrun aesthetics.
A flight-display interface inspired by F-14 Tomcat HUD instrumentation.
A woodland travel-journal interface inspired by The Lord of the Rings.
A spare mission-control interface inspired by the Endurance and TARS in Interstellar.
deckard.theme.description: Visual theme used by Deckard webviews.

deckard.zenMode.description: Turn Deckard's own chrome down: hide decorative labels and backdrops, thin the borders, and fold each row's file and line out of sight until the row is hovered or focused. Nothing is removed. Every control, count, and tag stays where it is, and works with any theme.

deckard.dashboard.openOnStartup.description: Open the Deckard Dashboard when VS Code starts in a workspace with indexed notes.

deckard.dailyNoteTemplate.description: Template used when creating a daily note.

deckard.weeklyNoteTemplate.description: Template used when creating a weekly note. {week} becomes the days it covers, such as 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-19, {date} its Sunday, and {month} that Sunday's month, such as September 2026.

deckard.monthlyNoteTemplate.description: Template used when creating a monthly note. {month} becomes the month, such as September 2026, {date} its first day, and {week} the days that month covers.

deckard.periodicNote.review.description: Write a review into a newly created weekly or monthly note: what was completed, what is still open, the notes written and changed, and the tags first seen in that period. Deckard: Write a Review writes or updates one whenever you ask.

enumDescriptions: Create today's note from the template alone.
Move the last daily note's unfinished tasks into today's note.
Copy them into today's note and leave them where they were.
deckard.dailyNote.rollover.description: What a newly created daily note does with the unfinished tasks of the last one. Deckard: Roll Unfinished Tasks Forward does the same thing whenever you ask for it.

deckard.dailyNote.rolloverDays.description: How many days back a rollover looks for unfinished tasks. 0 reaches as far back as your daily notes go, so a task left open before a week away still comes forward.

deckard.templatesFolder.description: Folder of note templates, relative to the workspace folder. Deckard: New Note from Template lists its Markdown files, and Deckard does not index them. Leave it empty to turn templates off.

deckard.exclude.markdownDescription: Glob patterns of files and folders Deckard leaves out of its index, written like `#files.exclude#`. Each pattern is relative to the workspace folder and applies when set to `true`, and a pattern that matches a folder leaves out everything in it. Deckard also leaves out what `#files.exclude#` hides.

enumDescriptions: A tagged line is a note of its own.
Only headings are notes. A tagged line keeps its tags and its place, and the heading holding it is what a search returns.
As Heading, except a line marked with a ^block-id, which stays a note of its own.
deckard.noteBoundaries.description: Where one note ends and the next begins inside a Markdown file. Tasks are always their own entry, wherever they are written.

deckard.parseInlineTags.description: Index tags on non-heading Markdown lines as standalone entries.

deckard.personMarker.description: Single-character marker for people. For example, set this to "~" to recognize ~mara-vale as a person.

deckard.entityNamespaceAliases.description: Maps one #namespace to another. Targets can be built-in or custom; for example, { "proj": "project", "leadership": "management" } treats #proj/atlas as a project and collapses #leadership/performance into #management/performance.

deckard.enableTagAutocomplete.description: Show indexed tag suggestions after a tag or people marker. Disable without affecting tag indexing, highlighting, or navigation.

enumDescriptions: Keep tags in related-note and tag-overview titles.
Remove tags from titles and show them as separate tag controls.
deckard.tagTitleDisplayMode.description: Choose whether tags stay inline in note titles or appear separately.

deckard.tagOverview.hubNoteExpanded.description: Show a tag's hub note open at the top of its page. When off, the hub starts collapsed to its title row; select the title to open it.

deckard.enableHeadingTagRelationships.description: Offer related tags, weighted by explicit co-occurrence and heading proximity, when refining a search of tags.

deckard.highlightNoteSections.description: Highlight indexed tagged note sections in Markdown editors.

deckard.editor.referenceCounts.description: Show, above the lines of a Markdown note, how many notes link to it, how many links name each heading, how many open tasks sit under each heading, and how many related entries Related Notes finds for each tagged heading.

deckard.editor.hoverPreviews.description: Preview the note or section a [[Wiki link]] points at when hovering it, and summarize a tag's entries when hovering the tag.

deckard.editor.linkDiagnostics.description: Mark a [[Wiki link]] that opens no note, because no note has its name or several do, and offer to create a missing note.

deckard.updateLinksOnRename.description: Rewrite every [[Wiki link]] that names a note by its old title when the note is renamed, in the same step as the rename, so one Undo takes back both.

enumDescriptions: Show a write that reaches more than one note in VS Code's refactor preview first.
Show every write that changes a note, however few it changes.
Apply writes without showing them first.
deckard.previewWorkspaceWrites.description: When renaming or merging a tag, and renaming a heading, show the changes in VS Code's refactor preview before they are written, where each one can be left out. Deckard: Undo Last Change takes back whatever was written.

deckard.editor.taskDependencies.description: Show, above a task with ⛔ or 🆔, how many open tasks it waits on and how many it holds up, and name a ⛔ id no task carries. A task with nothing open on either side shows nothing.

deckard.editor.dailyNoteActions.description: Show, above a daily note, links to the daily notes before and after it, and on today's note an action that carries in the unfinished tasks earlier daily notes still hold.

deckard.editor.linkProblems.description: Show, on a note's first line, how many of its [[Wiki links]] open no note, and an action that creates the notes the missing ones name. A note whose links all open a note shows nothing.

deckard.editor.embedProblems.description: Show, above an ![[embed]] the Markdown preview cannot draw, which heading or ^marker went missing, and open the note it names. An embed that draws shows nothing.

deckard.editor.unlinkedMentions.description: Show, on a note's first line, how many other notes write its title or an alias as plain text without linking to it, and an action that links them. A note no other note names shows nothing.

deckard.autoSelectNoteSections.description: Automatically show Related Notes for the tagged note section containing the cursor.

deckard.enableKeywordLinks.description: Let capped, section-scoped similarity of wording adjust the score of a related note that already shares a tag, association, or Wiki link. Shared wording never makes a note related on its own. Disable to rank by tags and links alone.

deckard.relatedNotesAssociationMinimumSu.description: Minimum distinct atomic source units required before a learned tag association affects Related Notes. One preserves intentional one-off associations.

deckard.relatedNotesRecencyHalfLifeDays.description: Optional Related Notes recency tie-breaker half-life in days. Zero disables it; daily-note and front-matter dates are preferred over filesystem dates.

deckard.tasks.addDoneDate.description: Add a completion date (✅ or [completion:: …]) when Deckard completes a task. Reopening the task removes it.

enumDescriptions: Obsidian Tasks emoji format, such as 📅 2026-09-20 ⏫ 🔁 every week.
Obsidian Tasks Dataview format, such as [due:: 2026-09-20] [priority:: high] [repeat:: every week].
deckard.tasks.metadataFormat.description: Format Deckard writes for a task that has no metadata yet, in / suggestions and completion dates. A task that already uses one format keeps it, and Deckard reads both.

deckard.tasks.assigneeFromPersonTag.description: Treat the first person named in a task's words as the person it is for, the way Deckard read tasks before the 👤 field existed. Off, only 👤 (or [assignee:: …]) says who a task is for, and a name in the sentence is a mention.

deckard.tasks.metadataSuggestions.description: Suggest due dates, priorities, repeat rules, and dependencies after typing / in a task.

deckard.me.description: Who you are in your notes, such as @ren-kade, so is:mine finds the tasks that name you as well as the ones for nobody in particular. Empty means is:mine finds only the latter.

deckard.statusBar.description: Show how many tasks are due today in the status bar, which opens the Tasks view when selected. The item is hidden while nothing is due.

deckard.taskReminderTime.patternErrorMessage: Write a time of day as HH:MM, or leave it empty for no reminder.
deckard.taskReminderTime.description: A time of day, such as 09:00, at which Deckard says how many tasks are due. Empty means no reminder.

enumDescriptions: Overdue, Today, and Upcoming.
Highest to lowest, with the tasks carrying no priority between.
The #status/… tag written on each task.
Who each task is for: the first person named on its line.
deckard.agenda.groupBy.description: What the Tasks view's groups are. The group control in its title sets the same thing.

deckard.agenda.upcomingDays.description: How many days ahead the Tasks view's Upcoming group looks for due, scheduled, and start dates.

deckard.agenda.query.description: A Deckard search that says which open tasks the Tasks view, Home's agenda, and the status bar's count are of, such as is:mine, or has:due OR has:scheduled OR has:start to leave out undated tasks. Empty means every open task.

deckard.board.statuses.description: Status columns on the task board, in order. A status found on a task but not listed here gets a column after them.

deckard.board.statusNamespace.description: Tag namespace that holds a task's status on the task board, so the default reads #status/doing.

deckard.outline.showTags.description: Show each heading's tags beside it in the Deckard Outline.

deckard.outline.followCursor.description: Select the Deckard Outline heading that contains the editor cursor.

deckard.outline.inheritedTags.description: Also show front-matter tags that every heading in the file inherits.

deckard.developerMode.description: Offer Deckard's own diagnostics, such as the related-notes ranking breakdown on a tagged entry's hover. Useful when tuning Related Notes; off for everyday note taking.

deckard.assistantTools.description: Let AI assistants in VS Code that use language model tools, such as GitHub Copilot in agent mode, search your notes and tasks with Deckard queries and list your tags. Deckard sends nothing anywhere itself; what a tool returns goes to the assistant that called it, which may send it to its own model service. VS Code asks you to allow the first call in each session.

deckard.mcpServer.enabled.description: Run a Model Context Protocol server on this computer, so Claude Code and other MCP clients can search your notes and tasks with Deckard queries and list your tags. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only and answers only requests that carry its token. Deckard: Copy MCP Server Setup copies the command that adds it to Claude Code.

deckard.mcpServer.port.description: The port Deckard's MCP server listens on, on 127.0.0.1.
